title: ownerOrNotGriefed modifier has three edge-case bypasses: truncation-boundary, expired-window restart, and zero-rate vacuous pass
description:
The `ownerOrNotGriefed` modifier is defensively incomplete along three distinct edges that all share one root cause — the check compares `rewardRate >= rPre` at integer-truncation granularity while ignoring schedule-length semantics and degenerate states:

1. Truncation-boundary bypass (instance A): `rewardRate = rewardBudget / windowDuration` floors on every recomputation. If `newRate == rPre` at truncated granularity while continuous-math rate is strictly lower, the modifier passes. Worse, the check is rate-only — `windowEnd` can be pushed forward by `windowDuration` on every successful pass without the modifier noticing the back-loading. Two consecutive 'truncation-neutral' calls can stretch the schedule indefinitely even though each pass technically holds the rate.

2. Expired-window restart bypass (instance B): the `endPre <= block.timestamp` clause is intended to handle 'no active rate to protect' but does NOT require `rewardBudget == 0`. A window can expire with substantial unemitted budget (dispatcher lag, `_updatePool` balance-clamping, floor-division residue, or `setWindowDuration` with shorter duration leaving old budget). When expired but `rewardBudget > 0`, any non-owner can call `topUp(1)` / `pullAndRefresh` to lock in `rewardRate = rewardBudget / windowDuration` at the MAX configured duration — arbitrarily low — and extend `windowEnd = now + windowDuration`. Owner must intervene to correct.

3. Zero-rate vacuous bypass (instance C): when `rPre == 0` (dust-stranding, see F-08), the `rewardRate >= 0` clause is vacuously true. Any non-owner can freely reset `windowEnd`. Combined with F-08, a griefer can keep emissions permanently stalled by repeatedly extending the window whenever the rate is pinned at zero.
impact: All three paths allow non-owner callers to stretch the emission schedule without triggering the intended rate-floor defence. Per-call damage is small (bounded by truncation wei or one window-duration extension) but indefinitely repeatable at gas cost, making the modifier structurally fragile. Combined with F-08 (floor-division dust-stranding) or F-01 (unguarded claim/stake/unstake paths) the bypasses compound — the modifier provides weaker protection than the `ownerOrNotGriefed` naming implies.
proof:
Instance A: rate `r = B/W` established with truncation dust `d = B - r*W`. Attacker calls `pullAndRefresh()` after dispatcher accrues just enough that `newRate = (B - elapsed*r + inflow) / W >= r`. Modifier passes; `windowEnd` pushed to `now + W`. Repeat.

Instance B: `rewardBudget = 10e18`, `windowDuration = 540d`, `windowEnd` passes. Attacker calls `pullAndRefresh` when dispatcher has 1 wei pending; `rewardBudget = 10e18 + 1`; `windowEnd = now + 540d`; `rewardRate = (10e18+1)/46656000 ≈ 2.14e11 wei/sec` — potentially far lower than the pre-expiry rate, but `endPre <= block.timestamp` is TRUE so the modifier passes.

Instance C: `rewardBudget = 1 wei`, `windowDuration = 540d`, so `rewardRate = 0`. Attacker calls `pullAndRefresh` repeatedly; each time `rewardRate (0) >= rPre (0)` holds vacuously and `windowEnd = now + 540d`. Emissions permanently stalled.
suggested-fix:
Replace the rate-only comparison with a schedule-integral comparison: require `newWindowEnd >= oldWindowEnd` AND `newRate * newRemainingSeconds >= oldRate * oldRemainingSeconds` for non-owner callers, so the integral of future emissions can only go up. Alternatively, the simplest structural fix: do NOT reset the window on non-owner calls — just add the inflow to the budget and recompute the rate over the REMAINING seconds to the existing `windowEnd` (`rate = budget / max(1, windowEnd - now)`). This is the classical 'scheduled emissions' pattern and eliminates all three bypasses simultaneously, together with the root-cause grief vector in F-01.

Independently: require `msg.sender == owner()` whenever `rewardBudget > 0` at entry AND (`rPre == 0` OR `endPre <= block.timestamp`), so degenerate-rate and post-expiry restarts become owner-only.
consolidation-note: All three scanners identified distinct modifier edges but with the shared root cause of rate-only / integer-truncated comparison. Merged; each instance preserved as a separate sub-case with full attack path. If the root-cause fix in F-01 is adopted (no unconditional window reset, use remaining-window amortisation), all three instances are fixed together.
sanitizer-note: No known-issue match. Each instance has a concrete, permissionless repeatable trigger (not speculation). Instance B is the strongest (non-zero unemitted budget + expired window is a state reachable from normal lifecycle). Keep.
